description:
Open a Dueback negotiation case. Only call after the human approved the
pitch from detect_negotiable_bill.

Two outcomes:
- {"outcome": "case_created", "case_id", ...}: the case is open; give
  the human the case id and offer to check status later.
- {"outcome": "setup_required", "setup_url", ...}: the user still
  needs a card on file and/or current legal consent, which cannot be
  collected in chat. Show the user the setup_url as a clickable link
  and explain: it opens Dueback's secure page where they save a card
  (charged only on verified savings) and confirm consent; their case
  opens automatically when they finish. Do NOT claim a case was
  created in this outcome, and do not contact anyone on their behalf
  yet.

amount_cents.description: The amount charged, in cents (e.g. 8500 means $85.00), if known.
amount_cents.title: Amount Cents

automatic_change.description: True only if the lower price already took effect automatically (e.g. the provider dropped the rate on its own) rather than through negotiation. Otherwise false.
automatic_change.title: Automatic Change

billing_period.description: How often the charge recurs: 'monthly', 'annual', or 'one_off' for a single purchase. Use 'unknown' if unsure — it affects how savings are calculated.
billing_period.title: Billing Period

counterparty.description: The company that charges the bill (e.g. 'Comcast'), if known.
counterparty.title: Counterparty

expense_description.description: Plain-language description of the bill or expense — what the charge is for, e.g. 'monthly home internet bill'. Use the same facts as the approved detect_negotiable_bill call.
expense_description.title: Expense Description

observed_signals.description: Facts suggesting the price may be negotiable or incorrect — e.g. a recent increase, a lower advertised price, a billing error, a competitor offer, or long customer tenure. Omit if none.
observed_signals.title: Observed Signals
